question: On patches of the not-all-equal weave without holes: is bond distance steps apart + 1 wherever a bond exists, and are the unbonded pairs exactly lone distinctions of opposite classes facing each other?

definitions.lone: a distinction in one knot of the patch
definitions.facing: z = x + p(u - x) + q(v - x), p, q >= 1, for x's knot {x, u, v}; both ways
definitions.D: least route weight, forward step 1, backward step 2

public_inputs.reused: BOND-METRIC's metriclib.py and NAE-METRIC's naelib.py, unchanged

forbidden_inputs: Changing cases, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
cheapest_meaningful_control: checks.py gates: the two-knot exhibit, the disc count, facing, the criterion on the two-knot base.

predictions.P0: the cyclic D-sum criterion gives the constrained sets (discs to 7 knots); D + D = 3 steps on every disc pair
predictions.P1: bonded pairs: b = steps + 1 (discs to 11 knots, 480 random discs)
predictions.P2: unbonded pairs are lone, opposite classes, facing each other
predictions.P3: facing pairs with no knot outside their parallelogram are unbonded
predictions.P4: parallelograms: exactly one unbonded pair, the lone pair
predictions.P5: a disc is metric exactly when it has no unbonded pair

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as scored by merge.py

stop_rule: One run; read-out; proof; referee hand-off; report.
